items: This is an inclusive, LGBT-friendly server. Hate speech and bigotry will not be tolerated.
You must be 18 years old or older to participate in this server.
No NSFW content.
No politically or religiously inflammatory material.
No advertising or spamming.
Be considerate of other people. Be excellent to each other.
We want this server to be a welcoming space! If you see something against the rules or something that makes you feel unsafe, let staff know.
Staff has the final say in what is considered disruptive behavior. If you have any questions, you are welcome to submit a ticket here: #Support

While evil characters are not inherently banned, there are certain behaviors that are unacceptable and not allowed by PCs on this server: any sexual or sexually motivated crimes, torture, intentional direct harm of innocents, engaging in slavery, and exploitation of others via mundane or magical means. Staff has the final say in determining whether behavior violates this rule and to what extent. Violations of this rule will be met with disciplinary action as determined by staff, up to and including immediate expulsion from the server.

blocks.text: (Throughout this document, there will occasionally be links to #Support. While you only have the @New Player role, this link will not work until you have a character approved in the #character-roster channel.)
Our goal is to provide players with an opportunity to create fun and unique characters by utilizing variant rules, and to give GMs the flexibility to create interesting and immersive stories.
Planet: Ao Hub City: Axiom

Axiom is what remains of an ancient civilization, its inhabitants lost to time. Long abandoned, it has become a place where those who are lost in this realm congregate to carve out a somewhat stable home. Though still threatened by the Convergence, it has managed to find some uneasy calm and equilibrium in the chaos around it. However, it is unclear how long this will last.
Deep within the city lives an enigmatic entity. This being, seemingly arbitrarily, creates and dispenses Wayfinders to the adventurers who have begun to congregate here.

There is much more lore to be discovered in Ao! Check out the “setting-lore” channel in the discord server - there, you’ll find lore on The Custodian, the Waygates, and some of the areas GMs have created for their sessions.
Largely as described in Dual-Class PCs, with the following clarifications/tweaks:

items: Choose a primary class. This will dictate your Key Ability Score boost for your character, as well as the Key Ability for that Class DC. (E.G; a Kineticist would choose Con, and have their Kineticist Class DC scale off Constitution.)
Choose a secondary class, and if applicable, determine the key ability score for that Class DC. (e.g. Fighter would choose between Dexterity or Strength for their Fighter Class DC).

blocks.text: THIS DOES NOT BOOST THE CHOSEN ABILITY SCORE. It is only used to determine your secondary Class DC.

items: Choose a free bonus ability score boost. You may boost any ability not already boosted by your primary class’s Key Ability Score.

blocks.text: Example: A Kineticist/Fighter boosts Constitution, and uses Constitution for their Kineticist Class DC, and chooses Dexterity for their Fighter Class DC. They may now choose to boost any of the other five abilities besides Constitution.

This essentially gives one fixed ability boost based on one class, and one floating. This follows Pathbuilder's implementation of Dual Class ability boosts, so if your ability scores work there, it should be correct.
We have Foundry automation to help correctly set up your Dual Class and ability boosts, so it’s easier than it sounds. Instructions on how to use these will be in the Character Creation section.

items: This variant rule is slightly altered. You may refer to Free Archetype, with the following modifications:

The first dedication feat taken in these slots is exempt from the rule that you must complete other archetypes with at least 3 feats before you can start another. For example, if you start an archetype with one of your level 2 class feats, you may start another one in the level 2 free archetype slot. Of those first two archetype dedications, only 1 may be a multiclass archetype (for example, you may take Chronoskimmer and Champion dedications, but not Champion and Rogue dedications). After the first dedication, normal rules for completing archetypes apply and you must complete all active archetypes before starting another.

blocks.text: e.g.; You may take Champion and Chronoskimmer archetypes at level 2, using a class feat and a Free Archetype feat slot. In order to take a third archetype, you must take an additional two feats from Champion and Chronoskimmer archetypes, such as Basic Devotion & Advanced Devotion and Turn Back the Clock & Guide the Timeline. Once you have taken your third archetype, you must follow the normal rules and take 2 feats out of that archetype in order to take a fourth.

items: If a specific archetype provides an exception to the requirement that prior archetypes must be completed with 3 feats, typically as a follow-on archetype to another, then that is allowed. For example, Scions of Domora may be taken if you have the Familiar Master archetype but haven’t taken two other feats from it, or Beastgunner without enough Spellshot Archetype feats.

blocks.text: e.g.; If you take Familiar Master at 2 with a normal class feat, you may still take Chronoskimmer at 2 with a FA feat. You will not normally be able to take another archetype until you have two feats from Familiar Master and Chronoskimmer; however, you will be able to take Scions of Domora due to having the Familiar Master dedication. After that, all archetypes need to be completed before starting another one.

Convergence has special rules about how Common, Uncommon and Rare items, classes, archetypes, features, spells and ancestries are treated, as well as some backgrounds and spells being blacklisted altogether.

As a general server rule, every character may be treated as having access to anything and everything with the Uncommon tag, and may treat anything with the Uncommon tag as Common for all other intents and purposes. For example, you may select an Uncommon weapon from the axe or weapon group as part of Surki Weapon Familiarity, instead of only Common. This also extends to any DC adjustments from Crafting. In short: Treat anything Uncommon as either Uncommon or Common, depending on whatever is most convenient for any given purpose.
For Rare, the following applies:

title: Rare Ancestries, Heritages, Classes, Class Features, Skill Feats

items: Battlezoo materials and Undead Ancestries/Archetypes require special consideration by staff.
Otherwise, all Rare Permitted unless blacklisted.
Exemplar archetype permitted
Otherwise, subject to approval by staff - may be subject to higher level of scrutiny.
Rare spells are not available by default and must be Learned as normal. Rare spells may be shared between players, or discovered in session.
Rare items and their formulae are not available for purchase by default. The items or their formulae may be discovered in session, or shared/traded between players.

The Convergence server has a number of house rules and rules tweaks. The following are mostly mechanical changes to how PF2e is played in session; crafting and downtime systems will be in a separate section. These house rules have the greatest impact on how you may decide to build your character.

Shattered Convergence uses an altered XP-based system. Rather than taking 1000XP to level up, and gaining experience in increments of tens or hundreds, you gain one XP per session played or GM’d.. You may also be rewarded XP for participation in certain server events. See the following table for XP per level:

items: You gain 1 XP per successfully completed session, GM’d session, and may gain XP in certain server events.

blocks.text: The “XP for next level” column indicates the XP required to level up based on the character level shown in the second column.

items: All Ancestry Lore feats give Additional Lore for the Lore they grant, bringing them in line with the remastered Ancestry Lore feats.
Kobolds characters may replace their ancestry language proficiency (Sakvroth) with Draconic.
Add Common to Conrasu languages known.
Add Kitsune to Kitsune languages known.

Any time you have a Versatile Heritage that has a language attached to it you may replace an ancestry language with one associated with your Versatile Heritage (e.g.; Goblin-Dwarf Versatile Heritage may replace Goblin language with Dwarven).
Merfolk’s Shore Gift ancestry feat is level 1, instead of level 9.
Unconventional Weaponry gives access, familiarity, and proficiency with any advanced weapon if you have proficiency with all martial weapons, not just ones tied to an ancestry or culture.
Samsaran’s Wanderer’s Soul feature does not apply to the Controlled Convergence ritual.
Dragon heritages: the magic tradition and breath weapon damage type of a dragon heritage may be changed, but not the breath weapon’s shape.
If you take the Stonemason’s Eye feat when already trained in crafting and when you already have the Specialty Crafting feat, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.

Weapon Specialization, Exemplar's Spirit Striking, and Runesmith’s Runic Optimization do not stack with each other. Upon gaining these features, choose which one to keep. You cannot change this choice in the future. This also applies to the Greater Weapon Specialization, Greater Spirit Striking, and Greater Runic Optimization class features.

In order to ease up on GM overhead, the Investigator feat That's Odd is banned. If you have chosen a Methodology or option that gives you That's Odd automatically (such as Empiricism), you instead gain a 1st level Investigator feat of your choice.
Summoner's Lifelink Surge loses the Vitality ("Positive") trait. This allows them to use it on their Undead Eidolons.
Swarm Eidolon’s Swarming Assault may ignore allies in the area.
Pre-remaster draconic bloodlines are allowed (Class).
Swashbuckler: replace the words “Dueling Parry” with “Extravagant Parry” in Dueling Dance. The requirements for the stance remain unaltered.
Shadow Sheath has some rules ambiguities by being a worn item that is in the Weapon Ikon category. To clarify what works with it:
Shadow sheath is a valid target for any weapon ikon feat for which the attuned weapon meets the requirements.
Attuned weapons lose any other ikon effects they have while in the Shadow Sheath.
The two halves of an Ikon created by the Twin Stars feat share the same limited use activations and cooldowns.
Barrow’s Edge and Scar of the Survivor may be altered to have the Void trait and give Void healing instead of Vitality.
Sorcerer’s level 10 class feat Ancestral Mage does allow casting spells gained through ancestry/ heritage when used in Sorcerer spell slots to gain a blood magic effect.
Inventor Weapon Innovation: remove the level 0 requirement (allowing the use of Barricade Buster, Gun Sword, etc.).
Giant’s Stature and Titan’s Stature from Giant Instinct Barbarian work even if you are already Large or Huge due to your ancestry or ancestry feats.
Thaumaturges may use Intelligence instead of Charisma when rolling Esoteric Lore.
For the sake of Kineticists interacting with Commander Tactics:
1-action Elemental Blasts may be treated as Strikes.
2-action Elemental Blasts may be treated as Cantrips.
Impulses may be treated as Spells cast from spell slots.
Ruffian Rogue may apply Sneak Attack to attacks made with non-finesse, non-agile unarmed attacks with a maximum damage die size of d6.
Sorcerer’s Blood Component Substitution replaces the Manipulate trait on spells with Concentrate.
Inventor’s Medium Armor Expertise feature at level 11 grants the Armor Specialization effect of a medium or heavy armor innovation (not “critical specialization”).
Titan’s Breaker may be a Brawling weapon that deals Bludgeoning damage, in addition to Clubs, Hammers, Axes, and melee unarmed attacks that deal Bludgeoning damage.

Replace the second paragraph of Thaumaturge’s Second Implement feature with: “While you're holding an implement in one hand, you can quickly switch it with another implement you're wearing to use Exploit Vulnerability, Intensify Vulnerability, or an action from or allowed by the implement you're switching to. To do so, you can Interact as a free action immediately before using Exploit Vulnerability, Intensify Vulnerability, or the implement's action. This allows you to meet requirements of having an implement in hand to use its action. For example, if you had your lantern implement in one hand, a weapon in the other, and a regalia implement you were wearing, you could swap your lantern for your regalia to use its Intensify Vulnerability. If you were holding a lantern implement and wearing a tome implement, you could swap your lantern for your tome to use the tome's free Recall Knowledge at the start of your turn. If you were holding a lantern implement and wearing an amulet implement, you could swap your lantern for your mirror to use Amulet's Abeyance.”

As written, this feature has some ambiguity as to what exactly allows swapping of implements. This change clarifies what you are allowed to use the free action swap for, as well as enhancing the usability of ‘passive’ implements, such as Regalia or Tome.

Fane’s Fouberie: If you are holding the deck of cards with both hands, you do not need to spend an action to draw a card. Any die size increases such as Deadly Simplicity apply to Fane’s Fouberie if it would apply to a dagger or darts. A deck of cards used for Fane’s Fouberie is a valid target for Champion’s Blessed Armament.

Battle Oracle’s Curse of the Mortal Warrior only suppresses resistance and immunity to negative effects from spells, not the temporary immunity that is applied by spells such as Guidance, Sure Strike, Blindness, or Shadow Projectile.
Investigator’s attack stratagem and Strategic Strike works with Alchemical Bombs.

Fuse Stance cannot be used to combine two stances with incompatible restrictions (such as each stance limiting you to only being able to make one kind of strike, e.g. Crane Stance and Gorilla Stance).

Group Taunt does not allow you to taunt additional targets with Taunting Strike or Armored Counterattack. If additional targets are already taunted, Group Taunt still allows you to keep up to three targets taunted when you use Taunting Strike or Armored Counterattack.

Wizard’s School of Gates has Interplanar Teleport replaced with Momentary Recovery, and Wizard’s School of the Boundary has Interplanar Teleport replaced with Devouring Void for their curriculum lists. Any other Bloodline, Arcane School, Apparition, or other similar subclass feature that grants Interplanar Teleport instead grants Momentary Recovery.
If you cast Amped Message with multiple targets in the same casting, such as with the enhanced version of Automaton’s Messenger feat, pick 1 target to gain the Amped benefits.
Animist: If you resurrect the familiar granted by Spirit Familiar, such as with Familiar’s Resurrection, you regain the associated apparition.
Runesmith:
Trace Rune can be used as 1 action on a creature or valid target within your hand’s reach, not only on adjacent targets.
Smithing Weapons allows you to Trace Rune as 1 action on a creature or valid target within the reach of your Smithing Weapon.
Engraving Maneuver allows you to Trace a Rune on the target of your trip, shove, or disarm.
If you use the Engraving Strike activity, on a successful Strike, you can Trace a Rune on a target within your weapon’s reach, even if they’d be outside your hand’s reach.
Cruonign, Rune of Leeching, only grants temp HP equal to the void damage done by the rune, not all the void damage done by the strike.
Necromancer:
Necromancers are able to learn spells & add them to their dirge to prepare, as other prepared casters may do. The wording of the feature was unclear; this was our interpretation.
You may select Osteo Armaments to be an ikon. When doing so, you must pick one weapon to gain the ikon’s effects; creating any other weapon will not benefit from the ikon.
Draining Strike only heals for the amount of spirit damage done by Draining Strike itself, not all the spirit damage done by the strike.
When Enemies or PCs have a Quickened action to Stride, they may use any movement type they have access to.
When you use a spell that grants a Battle Form (such as Animal Form), you may use your own unarmed attack modifier whether it is higher or not.
Wall of Stone cannot be used to make an enclosed box by walling a creature in and then placing a roof over it.
Bard Composition cantrips such as Courageous Anthem and Rallying Anthem are auras and behave as such.
Battleform Tweaks/Clarifications:
Special Statistics refers to attack modifiers, skill modifiers, AC, speeds, and damage (including the number of weapon damage dice, dice size, additional damage, and traits).

As such, Battleforms cannot benefit from damage bonuses such as Rage, Sneak Attack, Precise Strike, Weapon Property Runes, etc – anything that isn’t a circumstance or status bonus to damage. They can still benefit from non-activated weapon property runes, such as Rooting and Ghost Touch (including when as part of an Astral Rune).
Any resistances and weaknesses possessed by the PC are retained unless exceeded by the battleform.
Any senses a battleform provides are in addition to pre-existing senses.

While in a battleform, you are not considered to be wearing armor, and thus do not benefit from feats and features such as Armor Specialization, Guardian’s Armor, or Stalwart Defender’s Tenacious Stance.
You still benefit from non-activated armor property runes.
You may take two class archetypes if both class archetypes are for different classes. This still follows all other rules and restrictions of the modified free archetype used on this server.

For example, you could make a Barbarian/Ranger and take both the Bloodrager and Vindicator class archetypes, but you could not make a Witch/Wizard that takes both Runelord and War Mage class archetypes, or a Champion/Witch that takes the Flexible Spellcaster and Seneschal class archetypes.
You also could not make a Witch/Wizard that takes the Flexible Spellcaster class archetype for both Witch and Wizard, as you may not take the same feat twice unless otherwise stated.
If your character has an archetype that involves designating an ally in downtime to any benefit (e.g.; Sniping Duo), you may freely designate an ally in your party at the start of each session.

Student of Perfection/Jalmeri Heavenseeker: change the feats granted to the “Qi Spells” feat to be in-line with the Remaster. If you already have taken the Qi Spells feat then these dedications grant it again.. If you already have both Inner Upheaval and Qi Rush, then you instead take another level 1 Monk feat of your choice.
All requirements that list the Powerful Fist feature can be met by any feature or feat (class, ancestry/heritage or otherwise) that increases the damage die of your default d4 unarmed attack/fist.

Remove Cavalier Dedication’s requirement that the granted companion has the Mount special ability, as pledges are often up to GM interpretation. We do suggest though, if you go this route to use your companion as a mount to align with the dedication’s flavor even if it does not have the mount trait. Additionally, you cannot skip the 2 feat requirement to leave this dedication for another because of a pledge.
Add to end of Starlit Sentinel‘s dedication:

blocks.text: "Attacks with these bolts are Ranged attacks with the base weapon, using your weapon's melee attack modifier. They are affected by and count as having all traits, properties, and effects of and applied to the base weapon except for Two-Handed and Fatal, as they do not use the weapon's damage dice."

items: This means Starlit Bolts can benefit from things like Precise Strikes, but not from a Barbarian’s Rage damage.
Captain: All characters with the Captain archetype gain the benefits of Leader of All as part of the dedication.
Cathartic Mage: The Hatred emotion of Cathartic Mage is banned and not eligible to be chosen. The Love and Dedication emotions are modified as follows:
You may pick your emotional focus at the start of each session.
In order to foster a positive environment, whoever you choose as your emotional focus must consent to being chosen as such, regardless of the rules on emotional foci.
Hellknight: Shackles of Law does not upgrade the Grapple from a success to a critical success.
Provocator: Pin to the Spot only causes the Grappled condition on a normal hit, and the Restrained condition on a critical hit.

Spirit Warrior: Overwhelming Combination is usable with two-handed melee weapons with the finesse or agile traits. At the end of the Overwhelming Combination activity, add this line: "If you are wielding an agile or finesse melee weapon in two hands, you may make the Fist strike even if you don't have a hand free."
Archetype Oscillating Wave Psychics do gain the Conservation of Energy mechanic and must abide by it.
Spellshifter: Redirect Spell is banned. Change the critical success effect of Dismantle Spell to “As success, but the spell stays suppressed for 1 additional round.”
Necromancer archetype: Remove the manipulate trait from Necromancer dedication.

Flexible Spellcaster: You do not need to take 2 feats from Flexible Spellcaster in order to take another archetype, as there are no other feats in the archetype. Flexible Spellcaster may only be taken for a Cleric, Druid, Witch, or Wizard.
Any character can only have up to two total weapons or handwraps with talismans/spellhearts affixed to them at one time.

Any character may only have up to 3 of the same permanent magic item at a time (excluding armour and weapons). Different tiers of the same item (as in the case of spacious pouches, staves) will count toward this limit as if they were the same type of item, but items of the same type that function very differently (e.g. a Wand of Rank 2 Tailwind and a Wand of Blur, or an Aeon Stone (Preserving) and an Aeon Stone (Smoothing)) are treated as separate items for this limit.
All legacy dragon options are available including, but not limited to, class, ancestry, and gear options, including premaster Dragonhide materials.
For Handwraps, Amphisbaena Handwraps, Bloodknuckles, Dragon Handwraps: Replace Usage entry with Usage: Handwraps.
Despite the wording in the item description, Elixirs of Life also work on characters with the Undead trait.
Using the Shadow Signet activation spellshape does not stop “Magical Trickster” from functioning as long as the enemy is still off-guard.

All Ammunition Weapons gain the Alchemical trait while loaded and when using Alchemical Ammunition. They do not have this trait innately for the purposes of feats and synergies. (this primarily comes up when using a scatter weapon and/or using Alchemical ammunition and causing splash damage while an ally is wearing the “Backfire Mantle.” This is something a Paizo developer clarified during an old reddit discussion. This also works with regular black powder ammunition.)
The Essence Forge cannot be used to increase an item’s number of activations per day.

blocks.text: Additional changes noted in Crafting Rules (Deconstruct/Essence Forge).

items: Divide the Nail Bomb’s number of damage dice by two for the purposes of abilities that count the number of damage dice, such as Implement's Empowerment and Gravity Weapon, so as to maintain parity with other bombs.
The Sun Sight tattoo’s bonus to Perception checks is an Item bonus.
Backfire Mantle now applies resistance to all splash damage from yourself or allies.
The Stupefied condition from the Nightmare rune lasts for 1 round.
The Returning rune on a Windlass Bola works when used for a Ranged Trip.
Ice Gliders does not double your movement speed on Winter Sleet. Ice is an explicitly defined surface; Winter Sleet is not ice.
You may only benefit from one Elsie’s Excellent Bottled Vim at a time.
Legacy options that have not been reprinted are available, but if they were reprinted but function differently then you have to use the new option.

blocks.text: Example: Dragon Disciple, Kobold Breath.

items: In order to benefit from another PC's buffs, you must be in the session with them.

blocks.text: Example: Someone can only benefit from a Nymph (Battlezoo)'s Inspiration, the Fireproof spell, or the Harrowing ritual's buffs when in session with the character who produced the effects.

items: Regional lores give you a lore for a region that exists in the Convergence setting instead.

blocks.text: Example: When taking the Runescarred Archetype, instead of taking Thassilon Lore, someone might choose to take Axiom Lore, Floria Lore, or Agnivar Lore instead of Thassalon Lore. See the #setting-lore channel for ideas.

items: When an Animal Companion would increase in size due to maturity, you may choose for them to remain the same size instead. Megafauna are an exception: they cannot ignore size increases from maturity.
Learn a Spell tweaks:
On a failure or crit failure during the Learn a Spell downtime activity, you only need to wait until 12am Monday in your local time.

blocks.text: (You still lose the spent materials on a critical failure, and it costs 1 day of downtime no matter the rank.)

items: When using Learn a Spell Activity downtime, you may combine multiple rank 7 or lower Learn a Spell activities into a single day of downtime, so long as the combined Learn a Spell activities do not exceed 8 hours total time taken.

blocks.text: (This rule also affects ritual casting. Rituals still cost days of downtime spent and anything under 8hrs is one day, but multiple rituals can be combined as long as the total is 8 hours or less)

items: Bonded Animal has the following modifications and restrictions added:
Downtime required is reduced to 4 days.
You must have a way of keeping the animal Friendly/Helpful for the duration (Domesticated Animals are assumed to be always Friendly).
Target animal must be Common (NOT Uncommon).
Target animal must be at least two levels lower than the player (you may switch your Bonded Animal as necessary when downleveling).
Spells with missing stats:
Boneshaker’s enfeebled condition is missing a duration. Use a duration of 1 round.
Bloodsense and Sanguine Tenacity can be taken by any character even though they require “Blood Sensitivity” - although it is recommended players keep in mind the implications flavourwise.
Animal Companion Tweaks:
Fundamental Armor Runes may be inscribed onto Animal Companion Barding.
See the items tab of the hub foundry for the relevant items.
Barding is found under Items->Convergence Items->Barding.
This change allows non-Nimble animal companions to have comparable AC to Nimble animal companions.
Animal Companions may ignore the penalty for not sharing a language or not speaking a language when Demoralizing.
This change allows animal companions to make effective use of Intimidation proficiency and charisma scores.
Medium and Small PCs do not have their reach reduced when mounted on a Large or larger mount and wielding a Reach melee weapon.
This change brings Medium-on-Large PCs in line with Small-on-Medium and inherently Large PCs when it comes to Reach.
Animal companion features that scale off of an animal companion becoming Nimble or Savage will also scale off of any other Incredible option, such as Indomitable or Unseen.
For example, an Indomitable Riding Drake companion will still have their support benefit damage increased to 2d4.
This change allows players to pick the most fitting Incredible upgrade for their companions without missing expected progression for their choice.

Craft Anything can not be used to bypass the requirements of a Rare formula, a Rare material (such as Siccatite for a Siccatite weapon), a Rare spell (such as when crafting a Wand of Deep Sight), or a material sourced from a creature (such as Thunderbird feathers for a Storm Herald).

Adventurous Outfitter may not be used to progress crafting while on a session; you must still spend downtime to craft items and cannot use Adventurous Outfitter to bypass or reduce the downtime required.
Rare ancestries are not valid choices to take with Adopted Ancestry; you do not have access to them for that feat except for as detailed in the Controlled Convergence rebuild ritual.

Familiarity is defined as any feat or feature that reduces the required proficiency tier of a weapon. This includes Archer dedication, Mauler dedication, Intelligent Weapon’s Self Proficiency, Human’s Unconventional Weaponry, Undine’s Genie Weapon Familiarity, Kholo’s Kholo Weapon Familiarity, and any similar feats and features.
The creature targeted by Restraining Chains must attempt a Reflex save with the effects listed.

The Heartbond Ritual is an exception to the rule regarding benefitting from buffs provided by another player–you do not need to be in the same session as the primary caster of Heartbond in order to have and use the benefits of the ritual. Similarly, you are allowed to undergo a heartbond between two of the same player’s PCs.

blocks.text: The diversity of characters in Ao are vast, but not unlimited - in order to preserve the fantastical feel of the setting, there are some limitations and guidelines on your character’s backstory.

Characters must be from fantasy settings. There is only one known way into Ao: Convergence. Characters or places are plucked from their reality and dropped into Ao, the plane the city of Axiom resides in. Characters are therefore from a place that was converged, or were converged themselves.

Theming concessions for technology include magitech and steampunk, as well as any sufficiently-fantastical setting theme, but advanced technology like computers and motors must exist as a similarly fantastical or magical equivalent. (An intelligent crystal golem core in place of an AI, or steam-powered engines instead of electric motors, for instance.)
Real-world settings should be avoided. This includes alternate reality versions of real-world settings.
Automatons/Android characters need to adhere to the lore they were associated with. For example; Automatons and Androids both have humanoid souls and are not run or ruled by programming.
Characters must be at least 18 years old, regardless of ancestry.

Backstory: All characters must include a backstory that includes how you arrived in Ao. Usually this is done through a “Convergence Event.” A Convergence Event is when a piece of a world, or specifically certain persons of a world, are suddenly slammed into Ao, to become a part of this strange new world.

Alternatively, your character could have been born in Ao or even been created when two entirely different versions of them fused in a Convergence Event into what you are now. For example, Fleshwarps are very common in Ao, very created from a Convergence of multiple creatures into one entity.
Finally, characters should have a motivation and willingness to adventure, be part of a team, and take on the jobs and challenges Axiom has to offer!
During the submission of your first character please add the following phrase to the end of your submission, to confirm that you have read this page fully: “Kobold!”

Creating a character involves filling out a character sheet in the main Foundry server, submitting a ticket on Discord to have your character reviewed, and setting up your Convergence Character Tracker sheet. Follow these steps to submit a new character for the Convergence server. You may also refer to #character-submission in the Discord Server for more detailed instructions. Feel free to ask staff for help if you have any confusion or issues.

items: Load into the main Convergence Foundry Server at https://shatteredconvergence.org/join. (This link is also in #server-rules in the discord server).
Create a level 2 character sheet in the Character Creation folder, and fill it out as normal, with these notes:
Add a Dual Class class from the server’s items tab. If your class combination does not exist, ping staff.
Add a bonus ability boost item from the server’s items tab, as according to this server’s dual class rules.
Start with the following equipment:
45gp (which you may immediately start spending on common/uncommon level 0-2 equipment and items).
A free Convergence Wayfinder (from the server’s items tab).

title: Step 2: Create a character submission ticket

items: Go to #character-submissions, click “create ticket.”
Fill out ticket, using the example provided in #character-submissions.
Staff will review your character, correct any mistakes, and so on in the ticket before clearing it.
Make a copy of the character tracker (available in #resources) - this is what you will use to keep track of sessions, downtime, gold, and transactions.

blocks.text: It is required that you keep this up to date. Staff may request to review your character tracker for auditing, it may become necessary to rebuild your character if for whatever reason the sheet is lost or heavily outdated, it makes XP and downtime tracking much simpler - it is a very useful tool to keep maintained.

items: Create an entry in the #character-roster channel with your character’s info.
Sign up for sessions! Participate in RP! Join a guild! Character creation is done, now it’s time to actually play!

blocks.text: When starting out on Shattered Convergence, a player has three character slots. Additional character slots can be unlocked by progressing a character through different tiers, allowing more characters to be active at once. The first time a character for each player reaches the cap of Tier 4, and every tier afterwards, a new character slot is unlocked. For example, a player will start with 3 slots, unlock a 4th when a character reaches level 12, and a 5th when a character reaches level 15. These unlocks only happen the first time a player’s character reaches these levels, not on any subsequent characters (so getting a second character to level 12 will not unlock an additional slot). These unlocks are permanent, so even if a character dies or is retired, the player will retain access to these additional character slots.

You may completely rebuild your character before the character gains 5 XP post-creation - see Session Rewards for XP rules. Only XP from played sessions is counted for this; XP from GM’d sessions does not count towards the 5 XP limit.
Please submit your rebuild as a character submission ticket. You can do this once per character.
Here are some more guidelines on conduct for playing in Shattered Convergence, as well as some guidance on how singing up for and playing sessions works.
In addition to the server rules, the following behavior is expected during gameplay:
0.   Always target Alistair. 1. Be mindful of other people's time, show up on time and minimize distractions and delays during gameplay.
2. Be respectful. If there's a disagreement, the GM has the final say. Save extensive rules discussions for after the session.
3. Everyone is welcome to reach out to staff with concerns.

4. PvP is restricted and only with the consent of all participants (including the GM). For example, if you wish to cast a fireball that will also include your fellow party members in the effect, ask for permission first, and if they say no, then you cannot cast it on top of them.

Once you have at least one approved character through #new-character-submissions and have put them into the #character-roster, you can start signing up for sessions in the #voice-game-signup and/or #text-game-signup channels.

Please make sure to set the session time aside because frequent dropping from sessions can lead to GMs picking others over you. Please notify your GM as far in advance as possible if you cannot attend, as it can be quite difficult to change a player on the fly.

You will likely not want to manually rebuild and update your character on every GM’s table - keep your character sheet on the main Foundry server updated, and right click > Export, and use the downloaded .json to right click > Import into a character sheet on your current GM’s foundry server.

Players are encouraged to form groups together when they do not see a session available during a time in the day that they are available. We suggest you check out the Post Format post (in #looking for gm) in the discord server for more details.

You may apply for a session with a character that is higher or lower level than the GM’s chosen levels for the session. This is often because you are playing in a higher or lower Tier than your character is in- see Tiers for more information.

When you do so and are selected to join the session, your character will be temporarily Upleveled or Downleveled to meet the session level(s). You will receive session rewards appropriate to your character’s actual level, not at the level they are up/downlevelled to. Different GMs may have additional table rules for uplevelling or downlevelling characters, but at minimum you will be doing the following:

items: Uplevel: When uplevelling for a session, you acquire all features, feats, spells, formulae etc; exactly as if your character was naturally at that level.

blocks.text: In addition, you obtain any common/uncommon items you need to match the Automatic Bonus Progression bonuses for the level you are playing at. For example, if your character is level 2 and you are upleveling to 4, give yourself a Striking rune for one of your weapons, in addition to one item that will give you a +1 bonus to a skill.

In addition to items matching ABP, at levels 8, 10 and 16, you may add a property rune to one of your weapons. You may also replace all striking and weapon potency rune benefits with a staff or coda, at the same level as the highest-level weapon rune you would have otherwise received.
Finally, if your character would have the Shield Block feat at your uplevel, you may either gain a Reinforcing rune of your uplevel or lower, or a Sturdy shield of your uplevel or lower.
All benefits from uplevelling are strictly only for the duration of that session.

items: Downlevel: When downlevelling for a session, remove all features, feats and items that are above the level. You may replace overlevelled gear with a downgraded version that provides a similar effect; e.g. a Guise of the Smirking Devil could be downgraded to a Demon Mask for the session.

blocks.text: Once you finish upleveling or downleveling your character and have exported the sheet, move the sheet to the Trashbin folder on the main server. In order to reduce load times and lag, do not have more than 1 uplevel or downlevel sheet for your PC at a time.
Because the Battlezoo Foundry code is on the main server, but not necessarily on the server of the GM whose game you are joining, it is your responsibility to up level and down level correctly.

For Battlezoo characters specifically, we have created a folder in the main Foundry server called 'Up-Leveling' where you can import a temporary copy of your character sheet. This will allow you to temporarily change the level and fill out your feats without changing your permanent copy of your character sheet.

After you up level your character and give them all their feats and abilities, export it and bring it to the GM's game (right click character -> export character). There may be additional technical Foundry work required; ask staff for help. If you are unable or unwilling to up-level correctly, it is not the GM's responsibility to fix it, or to purchase premium 3rd party content for your convenience. Characters who are not properly upleveled by session start will have to run without the feats they would have gotten from the 3rd party modules.

As mentioned in Experience and Levelling, you gain Session Rewards for completing a session as a player or GM, and sometimes for participating in certain server events. Session Rewards refers to an amount of XP (as defined in Experience and Levelling), plus an amount of gold based on your level.

GMs may also reward bonus gold for a party’s performance or play exceeding expectations, up to an additional 20% of the standard gold reward. A GM’s Session Rewards will also include this bonus. If the party fails to accomplish the session objectives, however, they receive no XP. The GM may still give a reduced gold reward for partial completion of session objectives, but they are not required to.
Characters stop receiving XP once they reach the server’s current level cap (currently Lvl 12). This level cap will be increased gradually through server events.

Axiom has the resources available to remove lasting afflictions from its agents. When you return from a session, all lingering afflictions and conditions (Such as Doomed, Drained, etc.) gained from the session can be removed at no cost to you. If you do not wish to be cured, you may keep the affliction between sessions. We suggest, but do not require, that you keep and track afflictions in between sessions, especially if they are important to the lore/theming of the session or your character.
If you are afflicted by Resurrection Sickness, it is NOT removed this way; you MUST wait out the affliction timer.

If you would like to GM, select the Trial GM role in the #role-selection channel. You can become an official GM by running three different sessions while at least one Staff or Full GM is present to watch the session play out. Assuming they go well, you will be promoted to a full GM and will no longer need supervision. Additionally, the first 3 games you run on the server will grant you double rewards for your character.

When selecting players, we do not require you to pick first come first serve, but we suggest that you try to pick players that have not been in a session recently. Besides that, we suggest you try to pick a decently rounded-out party. The character tracker contains a template for players to post their characters’ classes, level, and how many sessions they have played in the last 7 days, as well as the date of the last session they’ve played.

After a session ends, all GMs involved in running the session receive gold and XP rewards as though they were a player who completed the session including bonuses, except any bonus downtime. If a GM has multiple characters, they choose which character receives these rewards.
GMs do not add any sessions they’ve GM’d to the number of sessions they’ve attended or signed up for that week.

A session should generally be 3-4 hours long and designed for 4-6 players. Sessions should be posted at least 3 days before they happen, though this is not strictly mandatory. This is to give players time to sign up.
There are two primary ways of creating a session:

1. Create a listing in either the Voice Game Signup or Text Game Signup channel respectively. The time of the listing should be specified using Hammertime if you have a specific time in mind, or When2Meet if the time and/or date is flexible. The listing must include the tier it will be run at and a brief description of the quest hook and basic objectives. Include trigger warnings for specific and intense triggers. These include, but are not limited to: Arachnophobia, slavery, sexual themes (remember the server rating regardless), and injury or death of minors. You must also use the session post format provided here.
2. Search through the Looking For GM channel, and find a game that you are willing to run. The same rules for running a game in this way apply as from above.

Characters are dual-classed, and as a result, are quite a bit stronger than normal PCs. When considering balancing, each PC should count as 1.5 PCs; A group of 4 should be balanced as if it were a group of 6, for instance. It is advised to use PF2Easy’s Encounter Builder for this purpose, averaging the level of the player characters. At very low levels (level 2-3), it may be advisable to ease on this additional encounter difficulty slightly.
When listing your game, the title should have the game’s tier first, then the date (MM/DD), then the name. The result should look like this:
5/19 T2 Saving Skrunkus
This lets applicants know the most pertinent information immediately.

It is not your goal as a GM to “win”; It is remarkably easy to “win” as a GM. Simply drop an ancient black dragon (or 20) on the players. You want to tell a story, and challenge the players without presenting them with totally unavoidable death. That isn’t to say there shouldn’t be danger or risk, and death may very well occur, but it is important not to be adversarial in your GMing. The players are not your enemy, and you are not theirs. We are all here to experience a story.

Additionally, it is encouraged to run games for everyone. This may not always be possible or preferable, but a GM should make an effort to involve everyone they can. This also means making players who have played fewer games a priority for sessions; We want everyone to get a chance to experience the story of the server.

If you coordinate with others to run a game outside of LFGM, please have a conversation expressing such on the Shattered Convergence discord server. It is absolutely okay if you coordinate outside of this, but please have something to point to if you post a game in voice-signups with a full roster.
Critical Hit and Critical Fumble decks are not allowed while GMing on Shattered Convergence.

Games should be run from Foundry, and this can be done either directly from your Foundry application on your PC, in which case your PC operates as the game server, or using Forge VTT, which handles the server operation for you.
This chapter mostly does not contain firm rules; rather, this is largely explanation and advice for how RP is facilitated on this server.

You may decide to have your character join a guild. There is no mechanical benefit, however it is a great way to encourage RP and relationship-building between characters, and often guilds will find special guild-specific sessions and host events for the server.

To establish a guild, you must fulfill these requirements: 1. The primary founder must be at least level 4. 2. The guild must have some theme, preferably not too similar to any pre-existing guilds. 3. Your guild must have at least two additional founding members belonging to two additional players (for a minimum of 3 members, including the primary founder) before the application is approvable by a Lore Master.
You may submit an application for a guild’s founding in the #guild-submission channel, where you can find a post “Submitting a Guild!” providing a framework for a guild submission.

Only active characters are able to be guild leaders; in the event of a character’s retirement, the guild must determine a new leader. In the event of a guild leader’s continued inactivity, the guild may determine a new leader for themselves.

Roleplay is, of course, very rules-light. You may find channels available to roleplay and seek fellow roleplayers in both text and voice in the Roleplay channel category in Discord. Many players use Tupperbox to facilitate RP, although this is not required.
Session rewards come in two main forms: Gold, and Session XP.

Gold rewards are calculated per player, based on their level. This calculator will tell you how much gold a player should get for session completion. Make a copy (File > Create a copy > Create a copy online) for use.

You can elect to hand out additional gold based on how well the players did, if they recovered extra resources, or for any other situation where players went above and beyond the mission parameters. This can be up to 20% extra gold, with the higher end being reserved for extraordinary feats.

Additionally, GMs may allow players to purchase a selection of game-relevant items at the end of the game, up to 3 items. These items will be purchasable at a 15% discount. There are enough copies of the items for each player to buy one of each if they wish (no need or greed necessary).
All players receive credit toward their next level; At tier 1, a player needs 2 completed sessions to level, at higher tiers, they need 3, 4 or 5. See Session Rewards/Levelling for more details.

When handing out rewards, do not ever release items that are made out of or require specific materials to be crafted. Rather, GMs should be rewarding the special material itself so that PCs are encouraged to use the player crafting system to get these special items made. Remember that all common/uncommon ‘minable’ materials can be directly purchased from NPCs, while all minable rare materials and all other materials have to be gained from session rewards.
Shattered Convergence also has some modifications to downtime and retraining rules, which can be found here.

Downtime is measured in “points of downtime”, where 1 point is equivalent to 1 day of downtime (8 hours). Every real-world week, at 12am Monday in your local time, each of your characters gains 7 points of downtime.
You may gain a bonus of 2 points for completing one or more of the following:

items: Once/week/character: Engage in RP. In order for a given RP scene to qualify for the bonus, you must engage in any of our #rp-rooms with at least 5 posts per qualifying participant, involving at least one other participant.

blocks.text: (Once complete, please ping @Lore master and @Trial Lore Master for approval.)

items: Once/session: Engage in RP or write a journal entry about a recent session (within 1 week of the session). RP subject to the same requirements as above. Journal entries must be at least two paragraphs long. Your character must have participated in the session.

blocks.text: You may bank as much downtime as you wish, however only up to 7 of your downtime points carry over when you level up your character. If you have any leftover downtime at lower levels, you MUST spend it as if your character was at that level, before spending downtime of any higher levels. If you wish to avoid the headache of tracking downtime across multiple levels, it is recommended you burn any leftover lower-level downtime as soon as you level up.
Each player is responsible for keeping track of their characters’ downtimes. Downtime is tracked on your Convergence Character Tracker sheet.
Spending downtime uses the normal rules in Pathfinder 2e. This can be anything from retraining, learning spells, casting rituals, crafting items, inventing formulas, and earning income.

Axiom is an energetic hub of the trades of goods and services, and as such any skills or lores may be used to Earn Income. We suggest that you come up with how your character is using that particular skill to earn income. Earned Income must be spent in batches of no larger than 7-day increments to represent a work week. Look here for the Earn Income Table.

To use any downtime option that requires a check, you have to use the /r feature in the Downtime bot-spam channel. It will not count if you do not fill out the modifier, DC, and description fields in the prompts. In the description field, we require you to list what skill you are using, what the downtime activity is, what rank you are doing it at. You also are required to fill the count prompt if you are doing multiple batches of checks with the same activity.

Downtime may be used for retraining feats, selectable class features, and other choices typically allowed by retraining, following the same rules for typical retraining in PF2e, apart from the following:

items: 4 days to retrain a Feat
4 days to retrain a skill increase
4 days to retrain a spell in a spell repertoire
7 days to retrain a class feature (e.g. Ranger Hunter’s Edge, Exemplar Ikon choice, etc)
7 days to retrain an ability boost
14 days to retrain from an ancestry’s base ability boosts to alternate boosts (e.g. +Str/+Wis/-Int/Free to Free/Free)

14 days to retrain a class feature + incompatible dependencies (e.g. if you retrain a Primal sorcerer bloodline to an Occult bloodline, you may also change your spells to suit the new spell list; or retraining Barbarian instinct + all instinct-dependent class feats)

When performing this 14 day retrain, you may replace any spells with ones of the same rank and may retrain skill boosts and skill feats tied to that retrain (e.g. a Primal sorcerer retraining to an Occult sorcerer may retrain Nature skill boosts and skill feats).

blocks.text: There is no monetary cost for retraining. Ancestry, Background, and Classes may not be retrained. For more complete overhauls of character choices such as these, use the Rebuild Ritual.
All instances of spending days of downtime must be posted in the Downtime Submissions channel, even if they do not require a check, along with which days you are spending for it.
We use the standard, newer rules for crafting from the remaster core book. See: PF2E Crafting Rules.
Crafters are also encouraged to post a thread in the character-owned-shops so players can easily find them and know what their offerings and discounts are from base values of items.

When making an item, just like any other downtime activity, it must be rolled (or detailed with assurance) in the Downtime bot spam and then posted with a link directing to the bot spam roll in the Downtime Submissions channel.

If your character has signature crafting they may optionally use it for each craft when they make the check. Any crafter can also choose or roll from the Item Quirks table for any item they craft, although these quirks cannot have any mechanical impact.
When crafting an item, it will usually have a final price lower than the original price of the item. This allows crafters to make a profit, even when selling items to players at a discount.

There are a number of crafting-related feats in PF2e, and many of them have been houseruled to add a discount to crafting costs. Refer to the Crafting Feats Cost Reduction Table to find these discounts - however, the discount may not exceed 30%. This does not change the cost or amounts of any Special Materials. The Specialty Crafting skill feat has been greatly modified - see the Specialty Crafting Rules for details.

Common/Uncommon items may still be purchased from NPCs at full price for convenience’s sake. However, NPCs cannot sell items that require a special material to craft unless that special material is common/uncommon, and either mineable (e.g. Quicksilver can be mined, Abysium can only be harvested from fallen asteroids) or farmable (most woods). This excludes monster parts and more obscure metals and stones.
Characters know all formulas for common and uncommon items by default. Rare formulas have to be gained through special mission rewards, and have to be approved by staff to be given out.

Anytime an item requires a special material that comes from an entity rather than something that could be mined, that material has to be acquired from session rewards. If the material doesn't list a price, then that material may be claimed from session rewards at no cost but each individual PC can only claim enough materials to craft exactly 1 item. “Rare” Mineable materials have to be acquired from session rewards, same as all rare items/formulae.

The Specialty Crafting table has been greatly altered, in order to make each specialty worthwhile to take. The altered table is as follows: Specialty Applicable Items Alchemy Grafts, Potions, and all items with the Alchemical trait. Artistry Armour: Natural/Innate armor. Fine art, including jewelry. Charms, Eyepieces, Medals, Spellhearts, Talismans, Tattoos, Whetstones (read the item descriptions), Equipment when made out of Porcelain (some masks). Runes etched onto any Artistry items. Blacksmithing Weapons: Groups: Axe, Dart, Firearm, Flail (except whips), Hammer, Knife, Pick, Sword. Armour: Groups: Chain, Composite, Plate (except Ceramic Plate) natural (Reinforced Chassis), Metal Shields (incl. Fortress Shield). Metal equipment. Runes etched onto any Blacksmithing items. Leatherworking Weapons: Sling group, Whips, Beastguns, Handwraps, Equipment from monster parts, leather weapons. Armour: Groups: Leather, Skeletal. Leather Lamellar, Equipment from monster parts, natural (Scales). Leather items, and any items made of cloth when made out of leather instead (most boots, gloves, some cloaks). Objects made from monster parts, e.g. Amphisbaena Handwraps. Runes etched onto any Leatherworking items. Stonemasonry Weapons: Groups: Hammer, Pick. Armor: Ceramic Plate, Fortress Shield. Gems, aeon stones, stone items. Runes into Stonemasonry items, Runestones of any Rune and onto any item. Tailoring Weapons: Handwraps. Armor: Cloth group, Robes. Cloth items, clothing, and any leather items when made out of thick cloth and similar materials instead (some boots, gloves, most cloaks etc.). Banners, Runes etched onto any Tailoring items. Woodworking Weapons: Groups: Axe, Bow, Club, Crossbow, Polearm, Spear. Armor: Groups: Wood, Skeletal. Wooden shields (incl. Tower, Fortress). Wood equipment. Scrolls, Wands, Staves, Grimoires. Runes etched onto any Woodworking items.
The following categories have been removed from the standard Specialty Crafting table, and their affected items split up into the following categories:
Removed speciality New speciality/ies Bookmaking Woodcarving/Artistry Glassmaking Alchemical/Artistry Pottery Artistry/Stonemasonry Shipbuilding Woodcarving Weaving Tailoring
SPECIFIC RULES FOR NON-WEAPONS/ARMOUR SPECIALISATION:

items: If the item’s description indicates a primary material, use that material to determine which specialty applies.
If an item could potentially be made of multiple materials (e.g. many masks), the crafter may decide which the primary material will be.
If an item could be made of a mix of different materials, lodge a support ticket to have a ruling made by staff.

When upgrading an item that was crafted with a speciality, you must use the speciality that was used to craft the item in the first place. This speciality cannot be changed, and the materials of the item cannot be changed later.
When crafting an item made with monster materials, Leatherworking is an optional specialty–you can always use the item’s default specialty (e.g. Amphisbaena Handwraps can be made with Tailoring).

title: Example of Crafting an Item and Determining its Specialty

blocks.text: Step 1: Does the item need a special material that cannot be mined, or is rare if it can be mined? Yes: Use the specialty of the material. No: Proceed to Step 2.
Step 3: Does the item list a specific material? Yes: Use the specialty of the material. No: Proceed to step 3.
Step 3: Is it a weapon or armor? Yes: Check the “weapon/armour types” sections of the Specialty Crafting table for the specialty. No: Proceed to step 4.
Step 4: Use the specialty that the item belongs to based on the above specialty list. ________________________________
The Deconstruct activity is permitted, with the below adjustments to the degrees of success (edits bolded and underlined).

items: Critical Success: If you are deconstructing the item to make a new, similar item, you can apply 70% of the cost of the deconstructed item to the new item. If you are deconstructing the item for raw materials alone, you can apply 60% of the cost of the deconstructed item to a single new item. In either case, if this is in excess of the new item's cost, the remainder is lost.
Success: As critical success, but you can only apply 60% of the deconstructed item's cost to the new similar item and 50% of the deconstructed item's cost to any single item.

blocks.text: A “similar item” will be defined as sharing the following:: 1. Major category (as seen on Archives of Nethys). 2. Specialty (as on Specialty Crafting Rules/Table). 3. Weapon/armour group (when applicable). 4. Usage (when applicable).

The Essence Forge cannot be used to create an item with increased activations. You may add any items that will fit in the receptacle as part of Prime the Forge - however, the value of any non-treasure items will be reduced to 60% for the sake of calculating the total value of the raw materials.

You may sell any item to another player at any price or even gift it to them for free. If the item has a level attached to it, then it cannot be used by the receiver of the gift unless the item’s level is within their tier.

You cannot use an item owned by another player’s character unless you are in a session with that character; creating a “Shared Storage” between two or more characters is not allowed. What you can do is buy an item from another character for a reasonable price (typically no less than 10% of the item’s cost.)
A player may not gift items between their own characters.

These rules are not exhaustive, but we hope the intent behind them is clear. Intentionally going against the spirit of these rules may draw the ire of the staff. Do not draw the ire of the staff. (Any form of guilt tripping to get lower prices or gifts is not permitted.)
Shattered Convergence has a system of player housing, giving people an option to spend their money in exchange for more minor benefits.

Housing can be found on the Housing tab of the character tracker, with a link to a master sheet showing all available housing options in the top left corner. In order to begin using housing, you will need to purchase Build Points (BP), which you can then spend to build rooms. Housing is tracked on the character level, with all of your characters needing to invest in housing themselves in order to obtain the benefits.

Each BP costs 1/3rd of a level’s total gold rewards, beginning at the total gold rewards of level 1 and increasing every 3 BP you purchase. You are capped at a maximum of 3 BP per character level of whichever character is purchasing BP.

BP will be spent on building various rooms, each of which have a cost tied to them, as well as other potential prerequisites and requirements. Each room also has a tier assigned to them, following Pathfinder’s proficiency tiers of Trained/Expert/Master/Legendary. In order to build a room of a given tier, you must have built at least two rooms of the tier below (for example, to build an Expert Kitchen, you must have built a Trained Kitchen and one other Trained room).

BP can never be lost, instead being allocated to rooms. 4 days of downtime can be spent to demolish a room and regain the allocated BP, allowing you to use it for another room. Additionally, once per session, you can take a free action to heal for 1/3rd of your BP rounded down or your character level in a session, whichever is lower.

In addition to the cost and tier, each room has a benefit of some kind tied to it. In most cases, this is a skill feat or general feat judged to be unimpactful enough to warrant being obtained through the housing system, such as Predict Weather, Sign Language, or A Home In Every Port. Housing can also be used to obtain extra known languages and certain Lore skills, such as Cooking Lore or Alcohol Lore. Housing also gives a character a once per session ability called “Thoughts of Home.” This ability can be used as a free action to heal for an amount equal to 1/3rd your BP rounded down or your current level in the session, whichever is lower. In the Convergence Items tab on the main foundry, you can find the Thoughts of Home ability and the corresponding Build Points item, which automatically scales the healing from Thoughts of Home.
Rituals are learned using the Learn a Spell activity as if they were spells of the same level, except that you do not need a Spellcasting class feature.

Certain feats reduce the cost of performing rituals: Ritualist Dedication: -15% Ritual Researcher: -10% Thaumaturgic Ritualist: -10% Additionally, secondary casters with any of these feats reduce the ritual’s cost by another 5% each. The maximum cost reduction for a ritual, regardless of applied discounts, is 25%.

This is a special Server Specific Ritual that was unlocked alongside the completion of the Convergence Laboratory Event in order to rebuild your character if you wish to do so. Using the research discovered in the laboratory and visiting the site in question one can potentially take advantage of the strange magic that the location is full of. Undergoing this ritual has little risk besides determining how long your debuff lasts thanks to the skills and mastery of our ritualists.

To begin you must submit your changes for approval. This involves having an updated Character Tracker and a before and after sheet on the main hub server for our sheet checkers to be able to review. Once that step is finished, submit your Controlled Convergence ticket through our character submission ticket system. As soon as that is approved you will need to source Ritualists to do the dice rolls for you. You may use NPCs to perform the ritual for you, but they will always achieve a Critical Failure result.

Once completed, you may rebuild any and every aspect of your character aside from backstory (as it is still the same character). You also gain access to your original ancestry for the purposes of Adopted Ancestry, even if it was Rare. This uses the same method and rules as the standard Reincarnate Ritual, with some modified costs and outcomes as follows:
Critical Success: The ritual succeeds with no complication. You may rebuild your character (while keeping the same backstory).

Success: As critical success, but your character needs a week to recover from the drastic changes that have occurred. Your character gains the Convergence Recovery effect with a duration of 7 (real-time) days, which causes Clumsy 2, Enfeebled 2, and Drained 2. You may re-attempt the ritual in order to erase this penalty by achieving a higher degree of success, but otherwise you may not reduce or remove this penalty by any other means (continued on next page) Failure: The ritual underwent more severe complications. As success, but the Convergence Recovery effect has a duration of 14 days. This duration can be reduced as your character rests and recovers in a medical environment, using 1 point of downtime per day. The duration cannot be reduced below 7 days in this way.
Critical Failure: The Convergence goes wild, and the backlash is severe. As failure, but the Convergence Recovery effect has a duration of 30 days.

Target Changes: Owing to the ritual’s purpose as a rebuild, the target of the ritual is changed to “1 living creature up to [x] level,” in accordance with the original Reincarnate ritual’s heightening. The target of this ritual cannot be one of the Primary or Secondary Casters.

Cost Changes: The costs of this ritual have changed, using the amount seen here and doubling the overall cost. This cost cannot be reduced like most other rituals. Specialized Ritualists may charge a “service fee” for their better dice rolls than an NPCs’, however this service fee cannot exceed the total income they could earn with 7 days of Earn Income (Success) each. You may also replace one or both of the secondary casters with an NPC but they always roll a critical failure. (i.e. group of Lvl 9 ritualists may not charge a service fee more than 21gp each. Which is lvl 9 earned Income 3gp x 7)

Reduction of the Debuff: A character may reduce the debuff length of time using their downtime days to recover in a medical environment at a 1:1 ratio. This debuff cannot be reduced to less than 7 days remaining without the result of a critical success from the ritual itself.

Recovery Period: Regardless of the result of the ritual, your character may not undergo the ritual again for 30 (real-time) days, except to re-attempt for a higher degree of success. ________________________________

Hopefully, you will not need to read these rules. Unfortunately, they may become necessary. In the event that a character dies in a session, it is possible to revive them, given the following rules and restrictions:

The character's body must be returned to Axiom. The character's body is considered returned if even one player character survives the mission, even if it would not make much in-universe sense for the body to be recoverable, even if the body was destroyed, and even if they were not depicted as bringing the body back in the session
In the event of a TPK, the party's bodies may be recovered by another adventuring party. Use the looking-for-GM channel to organize a daring group to do this. (See: Looking for GM Postings)

Another exception to the normal rules are Descents. Descents are a special type of high-risk, high-reward, high-difficulty combat-challenge session. One of the risks of joining a Descent is that in one, all character deaths are permanent (save for in-mission means of death prevention such as Breath of Life, Fish From The Fall's Edge, or Resuscitate).
Descents will always be clearly labeled as such in the game sign-up area, and will always include the rules for a Descent in their game description.

A spell or ritual must be used to revive the dead PC. If the mission ends within 3 in-universe days of the target's death, Raise Dead (Divine 6) may be used - the body is presumed to be magically preserved once it arrives in the stabilizing energies of Axiom, and Raise Dead may be used at the player's leisure. Otherwise, a Resurrect (Ritual 5) ritual must be performed.
Note: The Reincarnation (Ritual 3) ritual is currently banned, but has been repurposed as a means of retraining ancestry feats, heritages, or other normally-innate traits. See Controlled Convergence.

Resurrection costs must be paid by the PC being resurrected. The dead PC is allowed to pawn off their possessions at half market value (as per normal) to ensure they have the financial means to be revived. The caster must use 1 day of downtime for a Resurrect ritual, but not for a Raise Dead spell.
Dead PCs may not receive item gifts or GP; this is meant to prevent guilt-tripping behavior.

As per all player-run services in Convergence, PCs selling resurrection services may choose to add a service fee on top of the baseline ritual cost. We encourage PCs to be reasonable with any additional service fees.
The Resurrect ritual always brings the target back to life, but results of a Failure and Critical Failure apply additional penalties.
If the ritual fails, the target loses 2 levels. If the ritual critically fails, the target loses 3 levels. This is in addition to the effects of a Success.

50% of the ritual’s cost must be paid by the person being resurrected, in the form of raw gold. Services can be secured for this beforehand, but a character who cannot afford their ritual can sell items as normal to pay for it.

Coercion of other players to pay for the other half will not be tolerated in any capacity. You may ask and solicit others, but you cannot guilt trip them, threaten them, or otherwise try to push the issue if they do not agree to do so.

If a character dies but is not resurrected, a player may make a new character using the same slot. If so, they may elect to have that new character start at a level equal to half that of the original rounded up. Players may choose to start at level 2 instead. See below for starting wealth.

If you choose to retire a character, your character slot frees up. That character turns into an NPC and may be interacted with in sessions and text RP (though only with the original player's permission).

You also may have a character ‘retire’ as a part of a complete rebuild. In this case, the rebuilt character cannot be at all similar to the now retired character. A Retired PC cannot return to active duty without using a Rebuild, Retired Replacement, or using a Free Character Slot. Using the default rules for the chosen option.

After a character is retired, if a player makes a new character in that character slot, they may elect to have that new character start at a level equal to half that of the original rounded up. For example, a level 9 character that is retired may be replaced with a level 5 character. Players may choose to start at level 2 instead.
The starting gold for a new character is given by the Start Wealth Rounded column in this table.
